newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debt ends mixed, players eye key U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt ends mixed, players eye key U.S. data.

text.p: Emerging debt prices ended mixed in very light volume on Monday as players anxiously await Tuesday's key release of the U.S. employment cost index (ECI), Brady traders said.

"Generally spreads were mixed, but very little changed from Friday's levels," said one Brady trader. "The exception - Treasuries were up 11 ticks from Friday's close and our market didn't quite keep pace with it."
The benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond closed up 11/32 at 93-31/32 to yield 7.11 percent.

"ECI will be the most watched number among this week's batch of reports because it tells you almost directly what inflation is doing, whereas the payrolls number will indirectly give you an idea," another Brady trader said.
"It's clear that the labor market is tight, it's just not clear if that's feeding into inflation yet," he added.
In a Reuter poll, U.S. economists predict a 0.9 percent rise in the employment cost index versus a 0.8 percent gain in the prior report.

"Today's lacklustre action tells you that dealers are pretty happy with their positions right now," one trader said. "There was no real particular direction today...the Street's seems to be very comfortable ahead of tomorrows numbers."
The ECI report, as well as the remaining supply of economic data this week, will be closely scrutinized by market participants for any signs of inflationary pressures in the U.S. economy.
Market players said a string of stronger-than-expected economic reports could prompt the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), the Fed's policy-setting arm, to tighten its credit grip once more.
Last month, the FOMC voted to hike the key overnight lending rate by 25 basis points. Policy-makers are set to meet again on May 20.
Players said a strong report would trigger a selloff in the U.S. Treasury market which would in turn rattle Brady bonds.

Other reports due out on Tuesday are March durable goods and April consumer confidence. Later in the week, first quarter gross domestic product (GDP), April NAPM report, and April payrolls/unemployment figures, will be released.
In other news, players said the Mexicoan Peso was substantially weaker from Friday's levels, but no particular reason was given.
However, some cited a combination of end of month demand for dollars, and a fairly low overnight rate of 18 percent or so, and just general nervousness ahead of numbers in the U.S. this week.
"The Peso was weaker but it didn't affect Mexican Bradys too much," said one Brady trader.
Mexico Pars were unchanged at 70-1/2 bid while discounts were quoted off 1/8 to 87-1/2 bid.
Ecuador Pars and PDI bonds gained 3/8 to 42-1/8 bid and 58-1/4 bid, respectively. after news the government had decided to buyback some
"The market traded up after news on Friday that Ecuador would buyback $250 million of its par and pdi bonds, but there hasn't been a lot of folowthrough," said one Brady trader.
Among eastern european credits, Bulgaria Flrb were up 1/2 at 46-1/4 bid, IABs were up 5/8 to 61-1/2 bid. Russian VN US$ were unchanged at 78-3/4 bid.
